security_audit.summary: Six external-command findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline-code and fenced-code syntax; the document contains no shell backtick execution. The GitHub clone instruction is a confirmed low-severity supply-chain risk because it fetches mutable, unverified external content. No prompt injection or data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Pin installation to a reviewed commit or release, document checksum verification, and align subsequent paths with the cloned directory.

finding_verdicts.reason: The backticks on line 21 delimit the package name as Markdown inline code. They do not invoke a shell or interpolate any value.
The detected backticks open and close a fenced Bash example. Markdown fences are documentation syntax and do not execute the enclosed clone command automatically.
The detection begins at a closing Markdown fence and spans headings plus another opening fence. No backtick command substitution or executable Ruby syntax is present.
Line 29 opens a fenced Bash example containing fixed agent-manager commands. The fence cannot execute commands, and no dynamic value is interpolated into a shell.
The detected backticks are the closing fence for the command example. The remaining lines are prose and inline dependency names, not execution syntax.
The backticks only format the tmux and python3 dependency names as inline code. No command is invoked.
The prerequisite clones a mutable external GitHub repository without pinning a commit or verifying integrity. Later documented commands depend on downloaded code, creating low supply-chain exposure.

content.user_title: Manage Local CLI Agents with tmux
content.value_statement: Coordinating several local CLI agents manually makes task assignment, monitoring, and scheduling difficult. This skill provides tmux-based commands for starting, assigning, and observing agents.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to run multiple local CLI agents in separate tmux sessions.
Provides commands to check the environment and list configured agents.
Provides commands to start an agent and follow its monitor output.
Shows how to assign a workflow to a named agent through standard input.
Identifies the agents directory and supports cron-oriented recurring work.
limitations: Requires tmux, Python 3, and the separately cloned agent-manager repository.
Includes guidance only and does not bundle the referenced management scripts.
Does not document access controls, resource limits, failure recovery, or session isolation.
Requires environment-specific validation before scheduled or consequential operations.

use_cases.title: Parallel Development Agents
use_cases.description: Run independent coding tasks across separate local sessions while keeping each agent output isolated.

use_cases.title: Routine Repository Maintenance
use_cases.description: Assign recurring maintenance workflows and prepare controlled cron schedules for local repositories.

use_cases.title: Agent Fleet Observation
use_cases.description: List agents and follow session output during coordinated multi-agent work.

prompt_templates.title: Check Prerequisites
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the agent-manager doctor check. Report whether tmux, Python, and agent configuration are ready. Do not change anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a read-only environment check.

prompt_templates.title: List and Inspect Agents
prompt_templates.prompt: List configured agents, summarize their current states, and identify any agent needing attention. Do not start or stop sessions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Review the local agent fleet before assigning work.

prompt_templates.title: Start and Monitor an Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Start agent [AGENT_ID], then monitor its output. Confirm the session started and summarize errors without changing other agents.
prompt_templates.scenario: Launch one selected agent and inspect its startup.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate a Scheduled Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [WORKFLOW_FILE], assign it to [AGENT_ID], and propose a cron schedule. Ask before creating cron entries or modifying agent configuration.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare recurring work with explicit approval boundaries.

output_examples.input: Verify that this workstation can run the agent manager.
output_examples.output: Readiness review complete. Python 3 and tmux are available. Agent configuration was found under the expected directory.

output_examples.input: Start the development agent and watch for startup problems.
output_examples.output: Agent EMP_0001 started in its local session. Monitoring shows normal startup output and no reported errors.

output_examples.input: Assign the maintenance workflow to a worker and prepare a daily schedule.
output_examples.output: The workflow was assigned to EMP_0002. A daily schedule was proposed for review, but no cron entry was created.

best_practices: Run the doctor check before starting agents or assigning workflows.
Use explicit agent identifiers and review current state before every action.
Review workflows and obtain approval before cron or consequential operations.
anti_patterns: Do not include credentials or sensitive data in assignments or monitored output.
Do not start duplicate sessions without checking the current agent list.
Do not treat monitor output as proof that a workflow completed correctly.

faq.question: What does this skill manage?
faq.answer: It guides local CLI agent operations through an external agent manager, with tmux sessions for parallel work.

faq.question: Which dependencies are required?
faq.answer: The documented workflow requires tmux, Python 3, and the referenced agent-manager repository.

faq.question: Can it run agents on remote machines?
faq.answer: No remote workflow is documented. The skill describes local sessions only.

faq.question: Can it schedule recurring work?
faq.answer: It identifies cron-friendly scheduling as a use case. Review schedules and permissions before creating cron entries.

faq.question: Does it include the management scripts?
faq.answer: No. This package contains SKILL.md guidance and directs users to clone the separate agent-manager repository.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
